I have a need to build a SOHO file server for a startup. I've got a few unique challenges I'd like to bounce off the community.

  • Business is small but deals with financial data that has to be kept non-cloud with access controls.
  • Admin is more familiar with Windows-based file permissions.
  • Large data (30TB RAID 60).
  • 6 users need to access storage.
  • Needs to somehow be backed up offsite for disaster recovery/business continuity.

This is a short-term need (see: 2-3 years before being replaced with something else as the business changes), so I was tempted to just build a Windows file server. The data needs heavy access controls and compartmentalization. The biggest challenge is probably figuring out an economic way to backup 30TB of data.

Thoughts?
Discussion: Securing a SOHO NAS/File Server.

The individuals using the server will be from all over the world, and the data being housed cannot be trusted to any of the privacy-invading cloud platforms so it needs to remain "offline". This also means it needs to be either syncrhonized to more than one physical location or have an appropriately effective offsite data backup method.

Trusted encryption (see: not the garbage with known NSA-RNG exploited back-doors like Bitlocker, etc). File sharing (localized Drive/Box/etc), access controls, and VPN are the preliminary business needs for this data.

We’ve sorrow enough in the natural way, When it comes to burying Christian clay. Our loves are not given, but only lent, At compound interest of cent per cent. Though it is not always the case, I believe, That the longer we’ve kept ’em, the more do we grieve: For, when debts are payable, right or wrong, A short-time loan is as bad as a long—So why in—Heaven (before we are there) Should we give our hearts to a dog to tear?
